sections.overview: The Viviparous Eelpout is a coastal fish of northern European seas, including brackish waters.
sections.identification: Its body is long and eel-like, with a continuous dorsal, caudal and anal fin; its bones can be green.
sections.habitat: It stays close to the bottom in shallow coastal waters, especially among eelgrass or other seabed vegetation.
sections.diet: It feeds on small bottom-dwelling animals such as amphipods, molluscs, snails and small crustaceans.
sections.behavior: It is generally shy, especially in shallow water.
sections.reproduction: After internal fertilization, females give birth to live young in winter rather than laying eggs.
sections.ecology: Its site fidelity and sensitivity to pollution make it useful in monitoring coastal environmental contaminants.
sections.conservation: Fiskepleje reports a marked decline in Danish waters; this is a regional observation, not a global status.
